subject: general
question: Which of the following is the most reactive metal?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Potassium.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Potassium (K) is a most reactive metal and reacts vigorously with air and water.

 
 
• A large amount of heat is produced in their reaction.
 
• To avoid such accidents this metal is kept immersed in kerosene oil.
 
• Potassium undergoes a reaction with water similar to that of sodium; the products of the reaction are potassium hydroxide and hydrogen gas. 
 
• This reaction releases a great deal of heat energy, often igniting the hydrogen gas that is produced.
 
 
 
• Sodium (Na) and Lithium (Li) are also very reactive to air and water and need to be stored under oil to prevent them from reacting with gases in the air and water.
 
• Caesium (Cs) is the most reactive of all metals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Metals react with water and oxygen present in the air. 
 
• Metal with higher reactivity has vigorous reactions. 
 
• For example, sodium catches fire in the air, hence it is kept in kerosene oil. 
 
• Due to such reactivity of metals, most of the metals are not available in nature in a free state. 
 
• They are present in form of their compounds (oxides, carbonates, sulphides etc,)
 
• Few metals which are least reactive are available in a free state. 
 
• Such metals are gold, silver, Platinum
